Now the full pipeline runs in 19.5s for the max-size plan (8 Dijkstras on 262144 cells, 1M edges). But guard is None because peaks (6.6e12 as) exceed all guards (max g=7 ns = 7e9 as). Since guard is None, we skip the full 3-comp solve — so19.5s is for 8 single Dijkstras + calibration. That's ~2.4s per Dijkstra.

Now the worst case: when the guard IS selected (need the full run) AND then the audit runs in the same process. Let me make a case where the guard is safe: set reconfig 0 and guards bigger... guards must satisfy 2g < S = 128 → g ≤ 63. Peak is 6.6e12 as = 6.6e3 ns?? wait6.6e12 as = 6600 ns. So no g ≤ 63 can cover 6600 ns. To make a safe guard I need a smaller peak: reduce drift (e.g., drift 0, heat small) and hop values (small jitter/measurements). Let me tune: drift_ppb small (0..10), heat small extra, jitter 0..100, measurement slacks small. Then peak maybe ~1e6 as (1 ns)... let me compute: hop = (upper[a][b]+upper[b][a])/2 + jitter — with latent potentials and slack up to 1e9 ps, upper values can be ~1e9 ps = 1e15 as. That's way beyond any guard. For the peak to be ≤63 ns = 6.3e10 as, I need hop ≤ ~1e10 as = 1e4 ps and drift small. So measurements should be tight (slack ≤ 1e4 ps) and jitter ≤ 1e4.

Let me create build_big2 with tight calibration and small drift so the guard is selected, and time plan+audit in one process. This is the real worst case: 8 single runs + 1 triple run + warmup + matrix serialization + audit (peaks recomputed via cache! — since audit shares the same profile+fabric key, `_bounds` and `_full` caches are reused ✓).

Also test the case where the two requests have DIFFERENT fabrics (no cache reuse) — e.g., plan on fabric A and audit on fabric B — then it's 2×(8 runs + full) ≈ 40-60s. Hmm — that might exceed 90s! Let me measure.

Actually wait — in the cache: `get_model` keyed by (profile, fabric). Different fabrics → different models → recompute. Worst realistic batch: [plan(prof,fab), audit(prof,fab,proposal)] with same fabric ✓ cache hit. Or [audit, audit] with different proposals but same profile+fabric ✓ cache hit. Could the grader give plan and audit with different fabrics in one process? "Each process has 1-2 requests" — the batch presumably tests each feature; a plan and an audit on the same fabric is the natural pairing. But an adversarial pairing (plan on huge fabric + audit on another huge fabric) could take 2×25s = 50s+ if guard selected... Let me measure the guarded case first.
